findingDetails.title: The browser-first delivery gate cannot fail on a lost divider or a lost indent
findingDetails.scopeProof: inside the declared target, section 8 Browser-first page write, converter and report
findingDetails.claim: Set-based one-directional import diff plus unasserted counts cannot detect a lost repeated line or a lost indent
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Looked for an expected-value comparison of dividers, blocks or checklist count in the same section and for the blocking sentence to name one; found none.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A human could compare verify.dividers against the markdown; the document neither asks for it nor states an expected count.
findingDetails.confidence: high on mechanism, medium on frequency
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Amend :589 to name a count comparison as blocking, or print expected counts beside observed ones.

findingDetails.title: A `- - -` divider renders as a bullet reading `- -`
findingDetails.scopeProof: inside the declared target, converter branches in section 8
findingDetails.claim: The divider branch omits one of five spellings the same reference names, and the line falls through to the bullet branch
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked the converter stated contract at :391, which names only `* * *` and `---`, so the input is out of contract.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The `importDiff` set diff does catch the substitution, so the page is not silently delivered clean.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Not applicable, already at the floor.

findingDetails.title: The `--write` formatter inserts dividers from the original neighbour lookup
findingDetails.scopeProof: inside the declared target, the `--write` branch of the same validator
affectedSurfaceHints: AI Systems/z — Claude Project Sync Loop/validate-output-format.cjs:1742
findingDetails.claim: Two adjacent Mark-as-done lines each get their own upper and lower divider, producing the double divider the checker reports
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether a second `--write` run repairs the double divider; it does not, because both neighbours are then dividers and nothing is rewritten.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Consecutive Mark-as-done lines may never occur in a real deliverable, and the formatter cannot delete content by design.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Raise to P1 only if a real deliverable is shown with adjacent Mark-as-done lines.

findingDetails.title: The import normalizer exists in three copies that have already diverged
findingDetails.scopeProof: inside the declared target, section 8 of the same reference
findingDetails.claim: Three copies of norm/got serve three programs and their first lines already differ
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Compared the three copies line by line where they are visible; :579 folds four divider spellings and strips leading whitespace inside one line, :626 and :714 continue across lines.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The copies may agree in effect once their continuation lines are read, which was outside this budget.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Resolve to no-finding if the continuation lines prove the three copies normalise identically.
